title: OAuth Server Settings
description: Configure the OAuth 2.1 authorization server. Used by AI clients (Claude, Cursor) via dynamic registration and by third-party integrations (ActivePieces, Zapier) via admin-created static clients. Run tcms oauth:setup once to generate the RSA signing key pair before enabling.

enabled.label: Enable OAuth Server
enabled.help: Master switch for the OAuth 2.1 authorization server. When off, the OAuth discovery documents and endpoints return 404, so MCP clients that see a discoverable OAuth server (Claude, Claude Desktop) connect anonymously to the public tier instead of demanding a login. Turn off to run a public-only MCP site — access is then anonymous (public collections) or API key (admin). Existing access tokens expire naturally (default 1 hour) and cannot be refreshed.

dynamicRegistration.label: Allow Dynamic Registration
dynamicRegistration.help: Enable RFC 7591 self-registration at POST /oauth/register. On by default — MCP clients (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) need it to connect without manual setup. Self-registration alone never grants data access: a registered client still needs an admin to approve its consent screen, which marks the client as self-registered and shows where approval sends you. Registrations are rate-limited and unused ones are pruned after a day. Turn off to require an admin-created static client for every integration.

accessTokenTtl.label: Access Token Lifetime
accessTokenTtl.help: How long an access token is valid. Shorter = better security (revocation takes effect sooner) but more refresh round-trips. Default 1 hour is the common OAuth middle ground. A custom PHP DateInterval spec set in tcms.php (e.g. PT45M) is kept and shown as-is.

refreshTokenTtl.label: Refresh Token Lifetime
refreshTokenTtl.help: How long a refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens. After this, the user must re-authorize via the consent screen. Default 30 days. A custom PHP DateInterval spec set in tcms.php is kept and shown as-is.

authCodeTtl.label: Authorization Code Lifetime
authCodeTtl.help: How long an authorization code is valid before it must be exchanged for tokens. Short by design — the user is mid-flow. RFC 6749 §4.1.2 recommends 10 minutes maximum. Default 10 minutes.

tokenEndpointLimit.label: Token Endpoint Rate Limit (per minute)
tokenEndpointLimit.help: Maximum requests to /oauth/token per minute from a single IP. Protects against brute-force code exchange and runaway refresh loops. Applies to all callers (admin requests are NOT exempt). Set to 0 to disable. Default 60.

dynamicRegistrationLimit.label: Dynamic Registration Rate Limit (per hour)
dynamicRegistrationLimit.help: Maximum requests to /oauth/register per hour from a single IP. Dynamic registration is an unauthenticated endpoint that creates persistent server state, so it is throttled — but hosted AI clients (Claude, ChatGPT) register from their provider's shared backend IPs and register again on every connect attempt, so too low a limit locks those connectors out for the rest of the hour. Default 60/hour. Set to 0 to disable.
